subject: Observability onboarding: dashboards, trace hooks, and alert choreography for SkyLabs
messages:
From: Arielle Moore <arielle@skylabs.io>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@skylabs.io>, SkyLabs Oncall <oncall@skylabs.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Observability onboarding: dashboards & alert choreography for SkyLabs

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's ability to keep inference predictable across our mixed GPU fleet. We'd like to move to an onboarding planning step focused on production observability and operational handoff: dashboards, trace hooks for our request paths, an error taxonomy for model vs infra errors, and alert routing/runbooks for our oncall.

Quick context: SkyLabs runs inference via a mix of on-prem edge boxes and GCP; we currently push traces to Datadog via OpenTelemetry and maintain a fairly noisy alert set. We care about: 1) reducing noise and having clear ownership, 2) establishing a small set of dashboards for SLOs and tail-latency, and 3) documented runbooks for failover (fallback models, region routing).

Can we schedule a 90-minute kickoff workshop next week to align owners, agree on a minimal alert taxonomy, and hand over the initial runbook/dashboards templates? I attached our current alert inventory (skylabs-current-alerts.xlsx) — sorry it's a bit messy.

High-level asks for the workshop:
- Review current alerts and map to Redwood signal types
- Sketch 3 dashboards (SLO, latency tail, model degradation)
- Define error taxonomy and signal owners
- Draft alert routing and simple runbook steps per class

Available windows: Tue/Wed mornings PT preferred. If you want, loop in whoever owns runbooks on your side.

Thanks,
Arielle
Arielle Moore
Head of Platform Reliability, SkyLabs

---
Attachment: skylabs-current-alerts.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Moore <arielle@skylabs.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding: dashboards & alert choreography for SkyLabs

Hi Arielle — great outline, and thanks for the inventory. Tue/Wed mornings PT works for us.

Proposal: 90-minute remote workshop on Wednesday 25 Jul 2028 at 09:00 PT. Agenda (proposed):
1) 15m — Introductions + current telemetry landscape (SkyLabs)
2) 30m — Alert triage: map existing alerts to Redwood signal categories and priorities
3) 20m — Dashboard sketching: SLO, latency tail, model-quality metrics
4) 15m — Runbook templates & routing: owner assignments and play steps
5) 10m — Next steps & deliverables (who does what by when)

I'll bring a draft onboarding checklist and a dashboards template to speed things up (attached: redwood-onboard-checklist.docx, sky-dashboards-template.json). Laura will cover alert-routing patterns and Ben will speak to tracing hooks and sampling guidance.

If that time works, we'll send a calendar invite and a shared Drive folder for artifacts. Please add any specific people you want in the session (SRE, oncall lead, or product owner).

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood-onboard-checklist.docx (docx checklist)
Attachment: sky-dashboards-template.json (json template)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding: dashboards & alert choreography for SkyLabs

Looping in a few prep notes so we come in focused:
- Ben: please prepare a short note on trace-hook placement (model input path, post-inference latency markers, KV cache miss points). Keep the examples concrete (path names + span attributes).
- Ben + Sean: include recommended sampling and KV cache debug toggles we can propose to SkyLabs engineering (minimal perf impact).
- I'll take ownership of an alert taxonomy draft:
  * SEV-A: production-impacting (model crash, inference errors > threshold, region outage)
  * SEV-B: degradation (tail latency spikes, partial model degradation)
  * SEV-C: informational (increased retry rates, transient infra warnings)
- We should propose routing: SEV-A -> SkyLabs PagerDuty primary, SEV-B -> SkyLabs Slack #platform-alerts + Redwood Ops (watch-only), SEV-C -> email/daily digest.
- I'll bring two short runbook templates: 1) model-fallback (steps to switch to fallback model + smoke checks) and 2) region-failover checklist.

Also: let's ask SkyLabs for a sanitized sample trace (span ids and names) to use during the workshop. If they have any DoD for sensitive fields, confirm redaction.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Implementation Lead, Redwood Console
From: Arielle Moore <arielle@skylabs.io>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@skylabs.io>, SkyLabs Oncall <oncall@skylabs.io>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability onboarding: dashboards, trace hooks, and alert choreography for SkyLabs

Sean / Laura / Ben — Wed 25 Jul 09:00 PT confirmed. I've added Dev and our oncall lead to the invite.

Notes from our side:
- We'll sanitize and upload a representative trace and a reduced alerts sheet to the Drive folder you created: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cX-Onboarding-SkyLabs (you should have access).
- Dev will share the minimal RBAC constraints our security team requested (no secrets in traces).
- We accept your proposed taxonomy mapping; please bring the runbook templates as suggested.
- Outcome we want from the session: a prioritized list of 8-12 alerts to keep for the first month, an agreed owner matrix, and an initial runbook iteration for model-fallback.

After the workshop we'll expect a follow-up package: dashboards JSON, runbooks (markdown), and a one-week ramp play for alert tuning. Also flag any blockers that would require an SRE deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward.
Arielle
Arielle Moore
Head of Platform Reliability, SkyLabs

Attachment: none (we'll upload sanitized files to Drive)
